title: Incentivizing Information Acquisition
abstract: arXiv:2410.13978v5 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: I study a principal-agent model in which a principal hires an agent to collect information about an unknown continuous state. The agent acquires a signal whose distribution is centered around the state, controlling the signal's precision at a cost. The principal observes neither the precision nor the signal, but rather, using transfers that can depend on the state, incentivizes the agent to choose high precision and report the signal truthfully. I identify a sufficient and necessary condition on the agent's information structure which ensures that there exists an optimal transfer with a simple cutoff structure: the agent receives a fixed prize when his prediction is close enough to the state and receives nothing otherwise. This condition is mild and applies to all signal distributions commonly used in the literature.

translated_abstract: 我研究了一个委托-代理模型，其中委托人雇佣代理人来收集关于未知连续状态的信息。代理人获取一个分布以该状态为中心的信号，并以一定成本控制信号的精度。委托人既观察不到信号的精度也观察不到信号本身，而是通过可以依赖于状态的转移支付，激励代理人选择高精度并如实报告信号。我识别出了关于代理人信息结构的一个充分必要条件，该条件保证存在一个具有简单阈值结构的最优转移支付：当代理人的预测足够接近真实状态时，他将获得一笔固定奖金，否则一无所获。这一条件较为温和，适用于文献中常用的所有信号分布。
tldr: 该论文识别出一个温和的充分必要条件，证明在此条件下最优激励合同可采用简单的阈值结构，即代理人预测足够接近真实状态时获得固定奖金，否则一无所获。
en_tdlr: The paper identifies a mild necessary and sufficient condition under which the optimal incentive contract takes a simple cutoff form: the agent receives a fixed prize if his prediction is close enough to the true state and nothing otherwise.
